liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (3 reviews): Healy altered microphone sounds for this song, a common late-80s practice; Space section is described as melty, liquidy, and cool before the midi [11][12][19]
- **Iko Iko** (2 reviews): Listener describes the opening number as having a kick-ass delivery; Jerry nails the second solo, with vocals giving chills [12][22]
- **Picasso Moon** (1 review): Reviewer calls this version the worst Picasso Moon performance ever recorded [11]
- **Bird Song** (1 other source): Uploader notes a really nice set one closer performance [1]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Friend recommended this version, which the listener considers a great take [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-05-07.140949.AA-toaK1-416-flac2448** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 154 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd89-05-07.dsbd.stephens.10978.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 151 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [3]. Said about its sound: Listener praises the sound quality of this specific recording; Listener loves the balanced sound of this board; Recording sprouts legs and crawls along foggy, steamy terrain with wild vibes [14][17][18][19]
- **gd1989-05-07.sbd.owenbros-tetzeli.fix-3329.34771.reflac.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 151 min [8]
- **gd1989-05-07.sennme80.wklitz.watson.99567.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 136 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [10]. Said about its sound: Clear, upfront sound with amazingly nice bass from the OTS; Slight panning or adjustment happens during Iko Iko [21]

## Around the show

- Listener felt magic flowing from the band on this specific night [15]
- Band members, especially Jerry, Phil, and drummers, showed great energy [17]
- Pass is from that night, not May 6, 1989 [24]
- This soundboard is leagues better than the other source with speaker imbalance [16]
- This audience recording far surpasses the soundboard version [22]
- 1988 recordings were much better and used only Toa K1 microphones [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-05-07.140949.AA-toaK1-416-flac2448**: taped by Archival Audio; transferred by Archival Audio; source: Recorded and Mastered by ArchivalAudio, Ian Stoy; Master Audience cassette: Toa K1’s spaced about 30” (Pointed At The Stacks) + Sennheiser 416’s (or Sennheiser… [1]. Also: Tape recorded using a Sony MX-12 mixer, likely grey market [1]
- **gd89-05-07.dsbd.stephens.10978.sbeok.shnf**: source: DSBD > DAT [3]
- **gd1989-05-07.sbd.owenbros-tetzeli.fix-3329.34771.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: Fix of shnid 3329 [8]. Also: Tuning track merged with d1t10; shntool fixed sector boundaries on CD2; First two songs of set II moved to CD1 for fit [8]
- **gd1989-05-07.sennme80.wklitz.watson.99567.flac16**: taped by Keith Litzenberger; transferred by M. Watson; source: (ots) Sennheiser ME-80-> Marantz PMD-430 (Dolby B)-> Sony UX-S 90 x2 [10]. Also: Keith taped and M. Watson transferred the cassette to digital accurately [21]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Kirsten Michel: [1989-05-07 Frost Amphitheatre, Palo Alto, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1989-05-07-frost-amphitheatre-palo-alto-ca-usa/) [25]
- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1989-05-07 Rex Foundation Benefit - Frost Amphitheatre, Palo Alto, CA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/04/grateful-dead-1989-05-07-rex-foundation.html) [26]
- Poster by www.amazon.co.uk: [Frost Amphitheatre, Palo Alto, California May 7 1989: Amazon.co.uk: CDs & Vinyl](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Frost-Amphitheatre-Palo-Alto-California/dp/B01M9IPJXN) [27]
